title: Selvage Session Protocol — the session envelope
description: Every text frame is one JSON object, and one of three shapes: a request, a response, or an event. Valid against spec/PROTOCOL.md §4. The byte form is spec/CANONICAL.md §2.

clientMessage.title: request (client → server)
clientMessage.description: A request carries an `id` the server answers with, a `method`, and method-specific `params`. A request without an id is answered with `session.error` code `bad_message`. `params` absent is equivalent to `{}`.

id.description: Unique per connection. The response carries the same value, so it is the only correlation the wire has.

method.description: One of the method names of §5, or an `x.`-prefixed name, or any other name at all: an unknown method is answered with `unknown_method` and the connection stays open.

responseMessage.title: response (server → client)
responseMessage.description: Exactly one of `result` or `error` is present, and the response carries the id of the request it answers.

error.description: Present instead of `result`. `code` is machine-readable; `message` is not stable.

id.description: The id of the request being answered.

result.description: An object, `{}` when a method has nothing to return.

eventMessage.title: event (server → client)
eventMessage.description: Events carry no `id` and are not responses to anything. An event name a receiver does not know is ignored.

params.description: Flat, and specific to the event. See the `events.json` schemas for the known names.

serverMessage.description: A frame from the server: a response to a request, or an event.
